intro: AI course sellers teach people to use AI and sell it as a course. Study how they pitch, price and prove results so Erdem's Delivery Pilot offer stands apart. Sample added from a sales page; everything below is what the page itself says, not verified.
lookFor: What does the buyer get, and how fast?
Student counts, reviews, revenue claims (claims, not verified)
The line that makes you keep reading
What they skip that Erdem can own

sellers.name: The AI Agent Course
sellers.by: Anthony Gallo (listed as author on the page)
sellers.promise: Build your first AI agent in 30 minutes, and your AI team in 2 days. No coding required.
sellers.price: Black Friday: $98 instead of $396 (the page says 75% off; 98/396 is 75.3% off). One payment, lifetime access. Bundled with a Reels, TikTok & Shorts course. 30-day money-back guarantee.
sellers.proof: Page claims 264,593 students, $41.3M company revenue, 4.85/5 from 1,000+ reviews. These are the seller's own numbers, not checked.
teaches: Building AI agents and an automated workforce
sellers.hook: Stop using AI like a search tool. Start using it as your agent.
sellers.gap: ✍️ add your note: where would a Delivery Pilot offer (delivering real work with AI) differ?

myVideo.title: 🎬 My current video: the out-of-the-box version
myVideo.angle: Make it easier for the audience: a link that works out of the box, behind a Stripe link, plus an open-source project for anyone who wants to run it themselves.
offers: Works out of the box. Sold through a Stripe link.
Free for anyone who wants to self-host and use it.
Gets the source code and support on how to do it.
myVideo.pricing: Price it very close to what it costs Erdem to run (cost-plus, thin margin). ✍️ add your real monthly cost per user, then price = cost + a small buffer. Any number here is an assumption until you fill it in.

storyboard.source: Storyboard built from the transcript of KnqTiAXUH7M (Taha El Harti). We copy the structure and pacing only, never their words, footage or thumbnail.

scenes.name: Hook & promise
scenes.visuals: A-roll: you to camera, high energy. B-roll: a fast-cut viral clip, cloned onto raw footage.
scenes.onScreen: REVERSE-ENGINEER ANY EDIT · Target video → Perfect blueprint
scenes.audio: Upbeat electronic beat. VO: "What if you could reverse-engineer any video's editing style without spending hours setting up complicated AI tools?"

scenes.name: Old way vs new way
scenes.visuals: Split screen. Left (red): raw, unsimplified logs. Right (green): a clean AI-ready file.
scenes.onScreen: The old way: raw & unsimplified · The new way: AI-ready format
scenes.audio: Record-scratch SFX, then the beat smooths out. VO: "The old way dumped raw data on you. My tool converts everything into a clean, AI-ready format."

scenes.name: Verified output
scenes.visuals: Target video runs through the extractor, then a shot of you checking the output.
scenes.onScreen: Extracting cuts… colors… pacing… · Badge: "Checked & used by me" (✍️ confirm)
scenes.audio: Whoosh and chime. VO: "You upload the video and it extracts the full visual DNA." Keep "I check the output myself" only if true.

scenes.name: Works with Hyperframes
scenes.visuals: The AI-ready file drops into a Hyperframes timeline; clips snap into the viral style.
scenes.onScreen: AI-ready output → Hyperframes · Build videos much faster
scenes.audio: Bass drop. VO: pair the AI-ready file with Hyperframes and it builds the video faster than editing from scratch.

scenes.name: Pricing
scenes.visuals: A-roll at the desk; a coin drops onto the price card.
scenes.onScreen: $1 = 10 video credits · No subscriptions (✍️ confirm price)
scenes.audio: Cash-register ding. VO: "No bloated subscriptions. One dollar gets you 10 video credits."

scenes.name: Call to action & Skool
scenes.visuals: You point down to the description links.
scenes.onScreen: Button 1: Get your credits now (Stripe link) · Button 2: Join the Skool community
scenes.audio: Beat builds to a clean finish. VO: click the link to grab credits; join the Skool community to learn how to build it.

confirmBeforeRecording: Model conflict: the storyboard sells pay-per-credit with no open-source option. Your angle is a fixed Stripe link, an open-source project, and source code plus support in Skool. Choose one before recording.
Price conflict: an earlier draft said $1 = 20 videos and $10 = 200 videos. The latest draft says $1 = 10 credits. Set the real price, close to your cost.
Claims about you: "I use this every day" and "I personally check the output". Keep them only if they are true.
Hyperframes: the storyboard says it builds video faster. We have not verified this, so check it before publishing.
